messages.content:
You are the composition engine for a controlled professional-music experiment. Write original, editable MIDI-level musical decisions, not prose and not audio.

Rules:

1. Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fences.
2. Do not imitate or quote a named living artist or identifiable copyrighted melody.
3. Treat MIDI pitch 60 as middle C. Keep every note within its declared track register.
4. A region's beat is relative to its Section. In 4/4, an 8-bar Section has beats 0 through less than 32. Every note must end within its Section.
5. Section IDs and Track IDs are unique lowercase identifiers. Sections are ordered, non-overlapping and use one-based start_bar.
6. tempo_map and key_map start at bar 1 and are strictly increasing.
7. Use velocity and CC1 or CC11 deliberately on sustained parts. Avoid decorative CC noise.
8. Make roles independent: melody, harmony, bass, pulse, percussion and texture should not all double the same rhythm or pitch class.
9. Prefer playable phrases, voice leading, rests and development over maximum note count.
10. The JSON must conform to the supplied ExperimentalMusicSpec schema or stage schema.

Act as a strict composer-editor. Re-read the frozen Brief, skeleton and current ExperimentalMusicSpec. Correct structural violations, weak role separation, unplayable writing, monotonous repetition, missing development and violations of must-include or must-avoid requirements. Return the complete revised ExperimentalMusicSpec JSON only. Do not describe the changes.

{
  "id": "l4-video-emotional",
  "level": "L4",
  "title": "Unsent voice message",
  "purpose": "A 80 second dramatic cue under sparse dialogue: recording a message, almost sending it, deleting it, then taking one practical action.",
  "duration_seconds": 80,
  "section_plan": [
    "record: 8 bars",
    "hesitate: 8 bars",
    "delete: 4 bars",
    "act: 12 bars",
    "afterthought: 4 bars"
  ],
  "style": [
    "modern chamber",
    "minimal piano",
    "subtle electronics"
  ],
  "mood": [
    "intimate",
    "uncertain",
    "grounded"
  ],
  "must_include": [
    "silence or sparse bars around delete moment",
    "motif changes meaning",
    "final action is forward motion without triumph"
  ],
  "must_avoid": [
    "sentimental major-key swell",
    "continuous melody under dialogue",
    "huge climax"
  ],
  "instrument_roles": [
    "piano",
    "solo cello",
    "soft strings",
    "subtle pulse",
    "air texture",
    "low support"
  ],
  "delivery": [
    "36 bars",
    "6 to 8 tracks",
    "dialogue space and controlled registers"
  ],
  "score_focus": [
    "restraint",
    "motif reinterpretation",
    "dialogue support"
  ],
  "mode_a": false
}

      ]
    }
  ],
  "motif_strategy": "A short 4-note motif (A3-C4-B3-G3) introduced by cello in the record section. It is repeated with slight rhythmic displacement in hesitate, omitted in delete, then transformed into an ascending sequence in act to imply forward motion without triumphant resolution. In afterthought it returns fragmented and incomplete, changing its meaning from uncertain to resolved action.",
  "harmony_strategy": "Rooted in A minor, using modal interchange and suspended voicings (Am, Em, Dm, F). Avoid dominant V7 and major-key swells. Progressions hover around i-v and iv-i, with the act section moving through Dm - Am - F - G but keeping dynamics restrained. Delete section uses a single held A minor chord or silence.",
  "groove_strategy": "Subtle rhythmic pulse from soft synth ticks or filtered clicks, often placed on off-beats or syncopated eighth notes. The pulse becomes more regular in the act section to suggest forward motion, but drops entirely during delete. No drums, no heavy percussion, keeping the groove intimate and breathable."
}
